section: Environmental institutions - MoEFCC, CPCB and SPCBs, National Green Tribunal, National Biodiversity Authority
subsections: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB
CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP

accepted.s: The National Green Tribunal Act was passed on which date?
accepted.x: The National Green Tribunal Act was passed on 2 June 2010. The Tribunal was subsequently set up on 18 October 2010.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of enactment from the date of establishment.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the legal status of the National Green Tribunal?
o: A statutory body established under the NGT Act, 2010
A regulatory body established under the Environment Protection Act, 1986
An executive body created by the Ministry of Environment
A constitutional body established under Article 21
accepted.x: The National Green Tribunal is a statutory body created under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010; it is not a constitutional body.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory-versus-constitutional distinction.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the National Green Tribunal is to:
o: Conduct criminal trials relating to all offences in India
Replace all State Pollution Control Boards
Frame the Union Budget for environmental programmes
Provide effective and expeditious disposal of environmental cases and relief for environmental damage
accepted.x: The NGT deals with environmental protection, conservation of forests and natural resources, enforcement of environmental rights, and relief and compensation for environmental damage.
accepted.tq: Choose the option covering the tribunal’s complete statutory purpose.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Green Tribunal gives effect, in the environmental context, to the right to a healthy environment derived from:
accepted.x: The right to a healthy environment is read into the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution, and the NGT helps enforce this environmental right.
accepted.tq: Use the article-number trap in constitutional questions.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the procedure of the National Green Tribunal:
1. It is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
2. It is guided by the principles of natural justice.
3. It possesses the powers of a civil court.
4. It is required to dispose of cases within six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The NGT is not bound by the CPC, follows natural justice, has civil-court powers, and is expected to dispose of cases within six months.
accepted.tq: Check whether all procedural features belong to the same tribunal.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the Supreme Court within:
accepted.x: An appeal against an NGT order may be filed before the Supreme Court within 90 days.
accepted.tq: Identify the prescribed appellate limitation period.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a location of a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
accepted.x: Pune, Kolkata and Bhopal are locations of NGT zonal benches. Shillong is a circuit-bench location.
accepted.tq: Separate zonal-bench locations from circuit-bench locations.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Green Tribunal consists of a Chairperson along with:
o: Members of Parliament and representatives of SPCBs
accepted.x: The NGT comprises a Chairperson, Judicial Members and Expert Members. The number of Judicial and Expert Members is stated as 10 to 20 each.
accepted.tq: Test the statutory composition rather than the office-holder alone.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the stated current information, the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal is:
accepted.x: Justice Prakash Shrivastava is identified as the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal as of 8 September 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the current office-holder without confusing the office with a former Supreme Court office-holder.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following Acts:
1. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
2. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
3. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
4. Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
5. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
6. Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991
7. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
Which of the above constitute the stated seven Acts under the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
accepted.x: All seven listed Acts are included: the Water Act, Water Cess Act, Forest (Conservation) Act, Air Act, Environment (Protection) Act, Public Liability Insurance Act and Biological Diversity Act.
accepted.tq: Verify the complete statutory list rather than relying on only the major pollution Acts.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Green Tribunal from the Central Pollution Control Board?
o: The NGT sets emission standards, whereas the CPCB awards compensation.
The CPCB hears appeals against NGT orders in environmental disputes.
The NGT adjudicates disputes and awards compensation, whereas the CPCB regulates, sets standards and monitors pollution.
Both bodies perform exactly the same adjudicatory and regulatory functions.
accepted.x: The NGT is an adjudicatory body that decides environmental disputes and awards compensation. The CPCB is a regulatory body that sets standards, monitors pollution and advises the Centre.
accepted.tq: Separate adjudication from regulation by asking who performs the job.
accepted.sec: National Green Tribunal - Act, benches, purpose, composition, jurisdiction, NGT vs CPCB  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of the CPCB:
1. Air-pollution functions were added by the Air Act, 1981.
2. Its scope was widened by the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
3. It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Air Act added air-related functions, the Environment Protection Act widened its scope, and the CPCB functions as a statutory body under MoEFCC.
accepted.tq: Test a sequence of institutional expansion and administrative status.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Chairman of the Central Pollution Control Board is:
o: The Secretary-General of the National Green Tribunal
A full-time chairman nominated by the Central Government
The Chairperson of the National Biodiversity Authority
A part-time member elected by the State Boards
accepted.x: The CPCB has a full-time Chairman nominated by the Central Government.
accepted.tq: Identify the appointing authority and full-time status precisely.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which body is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework?
accepted.x: The CPCB is the body responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.
accepted.tq: Assign the enforcement function to the regulatory rather than adjudicatory body.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Air Monitoring Programme is commonly abbreviated as:
accepted.x: NAMP stands for the National Air Monitoring Programme. NCAP is the National Clean Air Programme, while CAAQMS refers to continuous ambient air quality monitoring systems.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar environmental monitoring abbreviations.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. National AQI — Launched in 2015
2. National AQI — Daily bulletins
3. CAAQMS — Real-time air monitoring
4. PRANA — Tracking of NCAP
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The National AQI was launched in 2015 and issues daily bulletins; CAAQMS provides real-time monitoring and PRANA tracks NCAP.
accepted.tq: Match each programme with its distinctive function or portal.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the stated national air-monitoring network?
accepted.x: The stated network covers 516 cities and has more than 1,400 stations, including real-time CAAQMS monitoring.
accepted.tq: Read paired figures in the correct city–station order.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The real-time monitoring system referred to in relation to the CPCB air-monitoring network is:
accepted.x: CAAQMS refers to the continuous ambient air quality monitoring system used for real-time air monitoring. RTWQMS is associated with water-quality monitoring.
accepted.tq: Separate air-monitoring and water-monitoring acronyms.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring System mentioned for the Ganga and Yamuna is abbreviated as:
accepted.x: RTWQMS stands for Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring System and is associated here with monitoring the Ganga and Yamuna.
accepted.tq: Use the water-related expansion of the abbreviation.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated coordinating or supporting function of the CPCB?
o: Adjudicating appeals against orders of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The CPCB coordinates SPCBs, provides technical help, supports research and training, and performs monitoring and regulatory functions. It does not adjudicate appeals against Supreme Court orders.
accepted.tq: Reject the judicial power wrongly attributed to a regulatory board.
accepted.sec: CPCB - setup, parent Act, chairman, functions, NAMP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Water Act and Air Act, Consent to Establish is required:
o: Before setting up the project or establishment
Only when an appeal is filed before the NGT
accepted.x: Consent to Establish must be obtained before setting up the establishment. Consent to Operate is required before production or discharge begins.
accepted.tq: Apply the chronological distinction between establishment and operation.
accepted.sec: SPCBs - APPCB, labs, enforcement, consents  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A factory has been constructed and is ready to begin production and discharge. Which consent is required at this stage?
accepted.x: Consent to Operate is required before production or discharge begins. Consent to Establish applies to the earlier stage of setting up the facility.
accepted.tq: Use the project-stage sequence to distinguish the two consents.
accepted.sec: SPCBs - APPCB, labs, enforcement, consents  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board:
1. It enforces the Water Act, Air Act and Environment Protection Act.
2. It enforces rules relating to hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste.
3. It issues siting guidelines and develops SOPs for marine outfalls and hazardous waste.
4. It promotes cleaner production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe stated APPCB responsibilities, including enforcement, waste-management rules, siting guidance, SOPs and cleaner production.
accepted.tq: Test the full range of State Board responsibilities rather than only its core Acts.
accepted.sec: SPCBs - APPCB, labs, enforcement, consents  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Computerised inspection by the APPCB is associated with:
accepted.x: The APPCB uses computerised inspection in connection with Ease of Doing Business initiatives.
accepted.tq: Match the administrative reform with the State Board function.
accepted.sec: SPCBs - APPCB, labs, enforcement, consents  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was intended primarily to provide for:
o: Strict liability for damage caused by hazardous-substance accidents
Setting up of State Pollution Control Boards
accepted.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 provided for strict liability in cases of damage resulting from hazardous-substance accidents.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the purpose of the NET Act from the appellate role of NEAA.
accepted.sec: NGT predecessors - NET Act 1995, NEAA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the fate of the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995?
o: It was brought into force and remains the principal environmental tribunal law.
It was converted into the National Biodiversity Authority Act.
It was replaced by the Water Act, 1974 without repeal.
It was never brought into force and was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.
accepted.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was never brought into force and was repealed by the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
accepted.tq: Use the fate-of-legislation trap: enacted does not necessarily mean brought into force.
accepted.sec: NGT predecessors - NET Act 1995, NEAA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the NEAA is correct?
o: It was replaced by the NGT and its Act was repealed in 2010.
It was never concerned with environmental clearances.
It was converted into the CPCB in 1988.
accepted.x: The National Environment Appellate Authority was replaced by the NGT, and the National Environment Appellate Authority Act was repealed in 2010.
accepted.tq: Track institutional succession and the repeal year.
accepted.sec: NGT predecessors - NET Act 1995, NEAA  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The NGT combines which two roles associated earlier with separate environmental institutions?
o: Original jurisdiction over environmental disputes and the appellate role of the NEAA
accepted.x: The NGT combines original jurisdiction over environmental disputes with the appellate role earlier performed by the NEAA.
accepted.tq: Link the predecessor authority’s appellate role with the NGT’s original jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: NGT predecessors - NET Act 1995, NEAA  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Ministry of Environment and Forests formed
B. Department of Environment created
C. Ministry renamed MoEFCC
D. Air-pollution functions added to CPCB by the Air Act
Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Department of Environment in 1980, Air Act in 1981, Ministry of Environment and Forests in 1985, and MoEFCC renaming in 2014.
accepted.tq: Place the dated institutional milestones from earliest to latest.
accepted.sec: MoEFCC - origin, formation, renaming  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change:
1. It receives 0.07% of the Union Budget according to the stated current information.
2. It is the nodal agency for India’s NR7 biodiversity report.
3. It runs Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct according to the stated current information: the allocation is 0.07%, MoEFCC is nodal for India’s NR7 biodiversity report, and it runs Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan.
accepted.tq: Combine current institutional facts while checking each statement independently.
accepted.sec: MoEFCC - origin, formation, renaming  [APPSC]
